newsitem.title: GERMANY: WestLB tips overweighting utility Bewag.
newsitem.headline: WestLB tips overweighting utility Bewag.

text.p: Analysts at WestLB have issued an "overweight" recommendation for state utility group Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag), as the city of Berlin gears up to fully privatise the company.
A buyer for the company might expect to pay up to 600 marks per share, with Berlin aming for maximum proceeds for the sale, WestLB said. Bewag's shares were up 9.50 marks at 489.50 marks on Friday.
"The strategic value of the largest supplier of direct heating in western Europe will probably be enormous for potential buyers," WestLB said.

WestLB also said that Bewag's profits should grow by at least 11 percent each year in the medium term thanks to massive costs cuts and other advantaages such as the fact that it has 47 percent fixed rate customers.
Berlin's government owns 50.8 percent of Bewag's capital and has been negotiating since last year to sell a 25.8 percent package.

A special Berlin Social Democrats (SPD) party conference earlier this week appears to have paved the way to also sell off the remaining 25 percent after delegates voted in favour of full privatisation.
A number of companies both German and foreign are reportedly interested in the Bewag stake, particularly German utilities Veba AG and Viag AG, which each owns 10 percent of bewag via a subsidiary.
"The German utilities will try everything to acquire at least a blocking majority," WestLB predicted.
Among the foreign providers reported to be keen to buy into Bewag, Southern Co of the U.S. was on Thursday tipped as the first U.S. bidder in a report in the Wall Street Journal Europe.
